text: We arrived at the hospital 45 minutes early with our elder mini schnauzer on January 2nd. He was having breathing issues the night before. It got so bad as we were trying to wait until they opened, our pup laid down in the seat to die. We carried him up near reception, and there was nobody around. At this point he was expelling liquid from his nose, and his heart stopped as we walked up near the critical care unit door. A cleaning employee went inside the CCU, and out came I believe his name was Leo. I told him that our pup wasn’t breathing, and his heart had just stopped. He grabbed him, and ran inside with him. A few moments later the Dr. came out, and said our pup was stabilized. A few moments later we were able to enter and see him. They had a breathing tube inserted, and his heart rate wasn’t ideal, but it was ok. We visited him each day as he was recovering, and we were able to bring him home yesterday January 6th. He has been doing great so far, and seems happy to be back home. The CCU staff are amazing, and we appreciate everything your staff did to save our pups life. 🙏🏼🙏🏼

text:
I visited this clinic for the first time because it’s close to my home. The visit was for anal gland expression and nail trimming for my dog.

The vet in charge, Dr. Ponlakrit, immediately told me that it’s “normal” for dogs to bleed during nail trimming and that I shouldn’t worry. I found this statement deeply concerning. I told him that my dog is 9 years old and has never bled from a nail trim before. I clearly said I did not want the nails cut too short and that just a little trim was enough.

Despite my request, he ignored me and tried to cut deeply. My dog was visibly scared and trembling. His technique was extremely poor, his hands were unsteady, and he didn’t even seem to understand where the nail ends and the skin begins. He clearly didn’t know how to use the tool properly, and a nurse had to assist him.

At that point, I asked him to stop and said I would go to another clinic. Shockingly, he continued and insisted again that bleeding is normal, and tried to trim more nails. I finally got angry. He then started drawing on paper to “explain” why nails bleed. I told him I already understood the anatomy — the issue is not the biology, but the fact that he was clearly unskilled, ignored my instructions, and tried to cut my dog’s nails too deeply anyway.

Unbelievably, I asked for an apology, but he refused, saying again that it’s “normal” and didn’t apologize at all. He told me he had been working for a year — which makes sense given how inexperienced and unprofessional he was. But even then, a simple apology would have helped. Instead, he acted rudely and without respect.

The fact that this hospital hires someone with such poor skills and judgment raises serious concerns. I shudder to think what might happen if he were in charge of a more serious medical issue.

I’m writing this review to warn others: if you visit this hospital, please be very cautious if you are assigned to Dr. Ponlakrit. For the safety of your pet, I strongly recommend you avoid him.
